To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have generated chicken cells resistant to avian leukosis viruses by disrupting the viral receptors using CRISPR/Cas-based genome editing.

the targeted disruption of the tva receptor gene in chicken cells using clustered regularly interspersed short palindromes (CRISPR) and CRISPR-associated protein (Cas9) technology results in resistance to avian leukosis subgroup A viruses, and that the same technology can be applied to sequentially target multiple viral receptors to generate cells resistant against multiple avian leukosis subgroups.
we have used a CRISPR/Cas-based strategy to sequentially disrupt three ALV receptors, TVA, tvb, and NHE1, in chicken fibroblasts to demonstrate that ALV subtypes A, B, J do not share receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel strategy for the generation of cells resistant to infection and replication of ALV subgroups.
the development of a CRISPR/Cas-based genome-editing strategy to generate chicken cell lines that are resistant to infection by ALVs of subgroups A, J, or B.
the generation of chicken cells resistant to ALV infection by targeted disruption of viral host receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TVA is a receptor for ALV subgroup A and that the receptors for ALV subgroup B and J are TVB and chNHE1, respectively, but the receptors for ALVs subgroups C and D have not yet been identified.
ALV subtypes do not share host cell receptors.
the ALV host receptor is not shared among the different ALV subgroups.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CRISPR/Cas system could be used to modify the host genome to generate cells resistant or sensitive to viral infection, depending on the target gene and its function.
we used CRISPR/Cas-based gene editing to disrupt the host receptor for each ALV subgroup, resulting in resistance to the respective virus.
ALV subtypes A, B, J do not share receptors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CRISPR/Cas-9-based disruption of viral receptor gene(s) can generate cells resistant to ALV infection.
the ALV subgroups do not use common receptors for infection.
we have developed a strategy to block multiple viruses using genome editing.
